correctness.rationale: At equal N, B=sum min(x_i,y_i)/N and H=2 sum x_i y_i/(sum x_i²+sum y_i²), both exact rationals, with every species positive. Canonicalize an ordered community comparison by sorting coordinate pairs and taking minimum under global community swap: exactly the quotient of joint species relabeling and pair swap. Independently generated all ordered positive compositions for every N=2..8 and k=2..N; exact Fraction arithmetic, not source verifier, produced canonical type counts 1,3,7,15,32,66,137 and within-richness unordered comparison tests 0,1,7,31,136,566,2357. Strict opposite rankings appeared only once, at N=8,k=4. Direct dot products verify A: B=5/8, H=13/22; C: B=1/2, H=3/5. Homogeneity of both formulas proves recurrence at all positive multiples N=8q independently of finite scaling tests. Exhaustion proves only first layer and universal N<=7, not classification for all larger N.

value.rationale: The two indices are canonical ecological community-comparison statistics and the least equal sample size that permits them to rank two community comparisons oppositely, with species richness held fixed and every species present, is a motivated finite-resolution invariant. The sharp lower bound, unique extremal comparison at N=8, and homogeneous recurrence give concrete mathematically reusable information for metric sensitivity analysis; exhaustive finite work is the theorem, not incidental numerical evidence.

final_claim: For two equal-total positive-count communities on a common species set, compare Bray-Curtis similarity B and Morisita-Horn similarity H. Two community-pair comparisons cannot have opposite strict rankings at N<=7; at N=8 the sole first-layer reversal up to joint relabeling/exchange occurs with richness four: (1,1,2,4) vs (1,4,2,1), B=5/8 H=13/22, compared to (1,1,3,3) vs (3,3,1,1), B=1/2 H=3/5; scaling gives examples at all N=8q.
limitations: Equal community census size, common species richness >=2, each community strictly positive for each species, these exact similarity normalizations.
The N=8 uniqueness does not classify larger unscaled inversions; original formulas and empirical metric disagreements are established prior work.
